newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes higher but gains trimmed late.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes higher but gains trimmed late.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed higher but gains were trimmed late amid talk some participants of a Kansas wheat crop tour were finding less freeze damage than anticipated, floor sources said.
Refco and Lind-Waldock each sold 600,000 to 700,000 bushels late as the market came off its highs, they added.
The tour, organized by the Wheat Quality Council, was in southwest Kansas on Wednesday, the region of Kansas expected to be the most severely impacted by last month's freeze.
There were early reports that up to 50 percent of the crop in the extreme south-west corner was damaged, but fields in other areas were less severely affected.
The initial rise was partly sparked by sentiment the market was oversold after its recent decline.
News Pakistan bought 329,000 tonnes of wheat overnight, including 282,000 tonnes from the U.S., was supportive.

News an Oklahoma crop tour, sponsored by Johnston Enterprises, put the state's production at 109.9 million bushels was also constructive. A survey of Oklahoma State University in late April forecast a crop of 121.34 bushels.
July wheat closed up three cents a bushel at $4.25.
Other months were up five to one cents.
